name: Ariva Phase 2: displays and advertising
description: Phase 2 (owner request 2026-10-06): split-screen passenger displays where one region always shows the queue and instructions and the other shows instructions or, where the site allows it, advertisements; instruction slides, an advertisement media library with safe uploads and two-person approval, playlists and scheduling, and proof of play. Built after the Phase 1 MVP stories and before the dev cluster release (backlog/prd-phase1.json ARV-137), on the same branch and pull request as the MVP (owner request: one pull request). Advertising is a per-site setting, off by default, because many border authorities do not allow it in immigration halls.

userStories.title: [E21] Display layouts: split screen with the queue always first
userStories.description: Passenger displays today show one full-screen queue view (ARV-058). A display can now use a split layout: region A always shows the queue (waits, bands, stale fallback) with instructions, region B shows instructions or, where allowed, advertisements. Layouts are configured per display. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-79, CWE-306, CWE-863.
acceptanceCriteria: A display has a layout: Full (today's view) or Split, with orientation (landscape left and right, portrait top and bottom), the queue region's share (between 50% and 75% of the screen) and region B's content mode (Instructions or Advertising); the default stays Full, so existing displays are unchanged

The queue region is never hidden, overlapped or shrunk below its share by region B; stale and degraded states (bands, fallback text) behave as in ARV-058 inside the region; region B failing to load never affects region A
Right to left layouts mirror correctly in Arabic; text stays readable at 1920x1080 and 1080x1920
Layout changes reach a running display through its existing refresh path without a restart, and are audited
Playwright: each layout and orientation at 1920x1080 and 1080x1920 in English and Arabic, region B failing, stale queue data; visual baselines for the split layouts
Permission: layout changes need the existing display configuration permission; [SiteScoped]; E2E authorization rows

userStories.title: [E21] Instruction slides for region B and the queue region
userStories.description: Managed instruction content: short multilingual slides (for example 'Have your passport open at the photo page', 'E-gates for UAE residents and GCC nationals', 'Remove hats and glasses') with a built-in icon set, assigned per site, zone or display and rotated in region B or shown under the queue. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-79, CWE-863.
acceptanceCriteria: Instruction slides have a title and body per language (Arabic, English, Portuguese, Swahili, and the site's languages), an icon from a built-in set (no uploaded markup), a display duration (5 to 60 s) and a scope (site, zone or display)
Text is plain text rendered by interpolation only (no HTML, no Markdown rendering to HTML); lengths capped; control characters refused
Region B rotates the slides that apply to the display in order; the queue region can pin one slide under the waits
Admin screen to create, order, preview (in each language, left to right and right to left) and retire slides; permission Display.Content.Manage; [SiteScoped]
Seed: a starter set of arrivals instructions for DMO and AUH-TA (if ARV-139a is done)

userStories.title: [E21] Advertising policy per site, off by default
userStories.description: Many border authorities do not allow commercial advertising in arrivals and immigration halls. Advertising is a site setting decided by the operator of the hall, off by default, and a licensed module flag (ARV-135 when it exists). With it off, region B can only show instructions, and the advertising screens and APIs refuse to act for that site. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-862, CWE-863, CWE-269.
acceptanceCriteria: Site setting AdvertisingAllowed (default false), changed only by a SystemAdministrator with step-up MFA, audited with who, when and the reason

With it false: a display cannot be set to region B Advertising, advertising APIs answer 403 for that site (or 404 where the site is outside the caller's scope), and running displays fall back to instructions within one refresh
Optional zone exclusions: advertising can be allowed for the site but excluded for chosen zones (for example the immigration hall) even when allowed elsewhere
E2E: policy off and on, zone exclusion, permission matrix rows

userStories.title: [E21] Advertisement image library with safe uploads and two-person approval
userStories.description: Upload and manage advertisement images through IFileStorage, typed by their bytes, re-encoded and size-capped, with a two-person approval before anything can play and an authenticated display fetch. Split from ARV-142 on 2026-10-17 (videos follow in ARV-142b). Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-434, CWE-79, CWE-22, CWE-863, CWE-400, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: Accepted types by content, not extension: PNG, JPEG and WebP images, re-encoded on upload (decoded and written anew) to strip metadata and active content, within a byte size and a pixel limit checked before anything is decoded; SVG, HTML, PDF, animated images, videos (until ARV-142b) and anything else refused
Stored under generated keys only (IFileStorage, never a path from the request), size capped on the endpoint and in the read, the upload rate limit policy applies (ARV-018 pattern)

Each item has an advertiser name, a campaign, a start and end date (the site's local dates), and a status Draft, Approved, Retired; only Approved items within their dates can play; approval needs Advertising.Approve and a person other than the uploader and the last person who changed the item; a change to an approved item sends it back to Draft; every change audited

New permissions Advertising.Manage and Advertising.Approve in the role mapping and security/permission-matrix.json; approving is a critical action (step-up MFA, security/critical-actions.json); [SiteScoped]; refused while the site's advertising policy is off (ARV-145)

Advertising endpoints live in Ariva.Api.Main/Controllers/AdminArea/Advertising (namespace ...Advertising) and carry [AdvertisingAllowed] (ARV-145: 403 while the site's policy is off, 404 outside the caller's sites; AdvertisingAllowedTests fails the build otherwise); the media a display player fetches is display-authenticated, so it checks the display's own site and zones with the advertising rule of ARV-145 (AdvertisingPolicyGuard) instead of the filter; every lookup of a media item by id is filtered by the route's siteCode and the caller's sites (another site's item answers 404, IDOR)

Displays fetch media through an authenticated display endpoint (display credentials, ARV-058), never a public URL: only an Approved item of the display's own site within its dates, while the display is set to advertising and the ARV-145 rule allows it for the display's zones; anything else answers 404

A media library on the displays screen: upload with advertiser, campaign and dates, preview, approve and retire, in English and Arabic; the approve action is not offered to the uploader or the last person who changed the item (the server is the authority)
E2E: upload attacks (polyglot, oversize, wrong type, path tricks), approval by the uploader refused, cross-site 404, display fetch without credentials 401

userStories.title: [E21] Advertisement videos: MP4 (H.264) and WebM within a configured length and size
userStories.description: Adds short videos to the advertisement library of ARV-142a: typed and checked by their container, length and size capped by configuration, metadata stripped, played by displays and previewed from an object URL of media fetched with credentials. Split from ARV-142 on 2026-10-17. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-434, CWE-79, CWE-400, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: Videos accepted by content: MP4 with H.264 video (AAC audio or none) and WebM with VP8, VP9 or AV1 video (Opus or Vorbis audio or none), up to a configured length and size; other codecs, files without a length, truncated files and data after the last top-level box or element refused
Metadata stripped without moving the media: MP4 user data, meta and uuid boxes become free space; WebM Tags, Attachments and Chapters become Void elements
Parsing is bounded: every box and element size checked against its parent and the file, nesting depth and element counts capped, nothing allocated from a declared size (CWE-400, CWE-120)

The library, statuses, approval, permissions, audit and display fetch of ARV-142a apply to videos unchanged; the player and the preview play a video from an object URL of the bytes fetched with credentials, so the CSP gains media-src 'self' blob: and no other source
E2E: video upload attacks (markup in a free box or after the last box, a polyglot, wrong codec, too long, oversize), approval and display fetch of a video

userStories.title: [E21] Playlists and scheduling for region B
userStories.description: Approved advertisements and instruction slides are arranged into playlists with time windows (for example peak arrival banks), item durations and share of airtime, assigned to displays or display groups, with instructions as the fallback whenever nothing is scheduled. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-863, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: A playlist has items (advertisement or instruction slide), each with a duration (5 to 60 s, videos play to their length up to a cap), an order and an optional weight; a schedule assigns playlists to displays or groups by day of week and time window in the site's time zone, stored in UTC
Rule: when the zone's queue is above a configured wait band (for example Long), region B can switch to instructions only (operator choice per display), so passengers see guidance when it matters most
Instructions are the fallback whenever no playlist applies, an item fails to load, or advertising is turned off

Playlist and schedule endpoints follow the ARV-145 convention (Controllers/AdminArea/Advertising, [AdvertisingAllowed]); a display receives advertising items only while the advertising rule of ARV-145 allows it for the display (the site allows it, saved against the published zone profile, none of its zones excluded), read on every refresh; every lookup of a playlist or schedule by id is filtered by the route's siteCode and the caller's sites (another site's answers 404, IDOR)
Display players receive the resolved playlist through their refresh path and keep a bounded local cache (count and bytes) so playback continues through a short network loss
Admin screens to build playlists and schedules with a timeline preview; permission Advertising.Manage; [SiteScoped]
Unit tests for schedule resolution (overlaps, time zone and daylight saving where the site has it, empty schedule), API E2E and Playwright tests

userStories.title: [E21] Proof of play recording and figures
userStories.description: Advertisers pay for airtime: each display records what it played, when and for how long, and the figures per campaign are computed for the advertising report, which moved to ARV-146 with report generation. Epic: Displays and advertising. CWEs to review: CWE-863, CWE-117, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: Display players report plays (item, start, duration, completed or interrupted) in batches through their authenticated endpoint; the server bounds batch size and rate and refuses plays for items not scheduled on that display
Plays are stored as a time series (versioned script, binary COPY) with retention set by a site setting

Figures per campaign, advertiser, display and day (plays, airtime, share of the scheduled airtime delivered) from a site-scoped service; the report, its permission (Advertising.Report) and the CSV export are ARV-146
No passenger data of any kind; counts of people near a screen are not collected
Unit, integration and API E2E tests including forged plays and oversized batches
